title: MAXX with the variant argument TRUE returns the text: strings rank above numbers
query: EVALUATE ROW ( "r", MAXX ( T, IF ( T[n] = 2, "x", T[n] ), TRUE ) )

source.quote: If the expression has variant or mixed value types such as text and number, then by default MAXX considers only numbers
source.supports: without the third argument only the numbers are compared; with it, the maximum over all values

source.quote: DAX considers Boolean values greater than string values, and string values greater than numeric or date/time values
source.supports: the rank of types in comparisons: numbers and dates lowest, then strings, then booleans

source.quote: If true, maximum value in col will be same as order by variant desc column
source.supports: with the third argument TRUE the maximum is the first value of a descending sort of all values

derivation: T[n] holds 1, 2, 3. The expression gives 1, "x", 3. With the variant argument TRUE all values compete. String values rank above numeric values, so the maximum is "x".
alternative: The ranking of strings above numbers is documented for comparison operators. If the variant order put numbers above text, the result would be 3.
notes: The column's type is not asserted (string or variant).
